what_it_proves: The parsed Schedule D bond population is close to the statutory bond base and can support residual tie-out work.
boundary: Not final accounting proof until residual difference is explained.
next_proof: Define final reconciliation tolerance and inspect residual continuation/subtotal candidates.

what_it_proves: Athene generated statutory net investment income against the extracted bond, mortgage, BA, and liquid asset base.
boundary: This is entity-level yield, not holding-level income or borrower cash receipt.
next_proof: Join Schedule D/BA holdings to income, disposals, impairments, and realized gain/loss schedules.

what_it_proves: The cash-flow statement supports most of the summary net investment income as cash-flow net investment income.
boundary: Cash-flow net investment income is not allocated to individual holdings.
next_proof: Normalize the page 18 income exhibit and test received-interest fields by Schedule D category.

what_it_proves: Collected investment income is close to earned investment income at the legal-entity level.
boundary: Collected/earned proximity does not prove collection by issuer or asset.
next_proof: Map collected and earned income categories to Schedule D, mortgage loan, and Schedule BA holdings.

what_it_proves: Other unaffiliated plus affiliated bond income is visible against the Schedule D bond base.
boundary: The statutory exhibit is category-level and does not assign income to CUSIPs.
next_proof: Separate affiliated, unaffiliated, issuer-credit, ABS, and other bond income where page detail allows.

what_it_proves: The page-18 collected bond category is reconstructed from Part 1 and Part 4/5 Schedule D received fields plus the page-18 footnote adjustment within $2.
boundary: This is a legal-entity statutory income reconciliation, not borrower remittance, liability-adjusted return, or Apollo common-owner cash.
next_proof: Carry the $2 source difference as tolerance and obtain liability-cost and named-settlement evidence.

what_it_proves: The same-period statutory line for interest and adjustments on contract or deposit-type contract funds can be compared with net investment income.
boundary: Mechanical residual is not a normalized spread, distributable cash, return, or Apollo owner residual.
next_proof: Allocate the burden by liability block and add expenses, hedges, taxes, capital charges, and owner claims.

what_it_proves: The statutory line-of-business schedules show the individual-annuity portion of the liability-interest-and-adjustments burden against the summary total.
boundary: The individual-annuity total still aggregates multiple product blocks and does not prove credited rates, asset allocation, or owner cash.
next_proof: Obtain product/reserve-block credited-rate, duration, surrender, hedge, and expense allocation detail.

what_it_proves: The statutory line-of-business schedules show the group-annuity portion of the liability-interest-and-adjustments burden against the summary total.
boundary: The group-annuity total does not identify contracts, credited rates, funding source, or legal-entity-to-Apollo cash.
next_proof: Obtain group-annuity block-level credited-rate and liability-cost detail.

what_it_proves: The statutory notes quantify a derivative asset population while describing indexed-annuity crediting and asset-liability mismatch hedge mechanisms.
boundary: Gross derivative assets are not hedge cost, cash settlement, hedge effectiveness, product allocation, or owner cash.
next_proof: Join Schedule DB positions, derivative cash flows, gains/losses, and product or liability-block allocation.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part A shows consideration received or paid on terminations against the displayed ending book/adjusted carrying value.
boundary: This is a derivative turnover screen, not net hedge return, policyholder cost, parent receipt, or owner cash.
next_proof: Match terminated contracts to counterparties, premiums, collateral, hedged items, liability purpose, and cash-flow classifications.

what_it_proves: Mortgage-loan income is visible against the first-lien mortgage-loan base.
boundary: This does not identify borrowers or loan-level repayment behavior.
next_proof: Locate mortgage loan schedules and repayment/maturity detail if available.

what_it_proves: The cash-flow statement shows large proceeds from bonds sold, matured, or repaid.
boundary: Not matched to Schedule D Part 4 disposal rows or realized gains/losses by asset.
next_proof: Extract Schedule D Part 4 and match disposal proceeds to CUSIP/issuer where possible.

what_it_proves: The cash-flow statement shows material mortgage-loan proceeds from sale, maturity, or repayment.
next_proof: Extract mortgage loan disposal/repayment schedules if available.

what_it_proves: The extracted core invested asset base is larger than the life reserve plus deposit-type liability base.
boundary: This is not liability-cost, duration, credited-rate, or spread proof.
next_proof: Extract reserve interest, deposit-type contract cost, credited rates, surrender behavior, and ALM detail.

what_it_proves: The asset valuation reserve gives a legal-entity credit/equity risk reserve scale against invested assets.
boundary: AVR is not issuer-level loss or realized cash return.
next_proof: Join AVR components to NAIC distribution and impairments.

what_it_proves: The IMR scale is visible against bond sale/maturity/repayment proceeds.
boundary: IMR does not itself identify the sold holdings or realized gains/losses.
next_proof: Extract Schedule D Part 4 realized gain/loss rows.

what_it_proves: Current-year OTTI is visible against the Schedule D bond base.
boundary: OTTI is not yet assigned to issuers or borrowers.
next_proof: Locate issuer-level impairment detail and join to Schedule D holdings.
